proposed_widenings.name: modify_damage_roll
proposed_widenings.justification: The item grants a persistent bonus to weapon damage rolls made with the staff itself. The current surface can modify attack rolls, saving throws, AC, speed, and similar values, but it has no effect atom for passive damage-roll bonuses.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This staff has 20 charges and can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it.

proposed_widenings.name: weapon_filter.item_identity
proposed_widenings.justification: The current WeaponFilter only distinguishes melee vs ranged weapons. Staff of Power's weapon bonus applies only to attacks made with this specific staff, not to all melee weapons.
proposed_widenings.evidence: This staff has 20 charges and can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it.

proposed_widenings.name: modify_roll_numeric.on = spell_attack_roll
proposed_widenings.justification: The item separately grants +2 to spell attack rolls while held. The current RollKind vocabulary has attack_roll, saving_throw, ability_check, initiative, and death_saving_throw, but no way to target spell attack rolls without also catching weapon attack rolls.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While holding it, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class, saving throws, and spell attack rolls.

proposed_widenings.name: magic_item_attunement_restriction.by_class
proposed_widenings.justification: MagicItemRecord only records a boolean attunement flag. Staff of Power restricts attunement to specific classes, which affects who can benefit from all of its properties.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Staff, Very Rare (Requires Attunement by a Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard)

proposed_widenings.name: item_destruction.last_charge_outcomes
proposed_widenings.justification: The current last-charge policy only supports binary destruction on a die result. Staff of Power instead has two nonstandard outcomes: partial property loss on a 1 and charge restoration on a 20.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff retains its +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls but loses all other properties. On a 20, the staff regains 1d8 + 2 charges.

proposed_widenings.name: resource_spent.multiplier
proposed_widenings.justification: Retributive Strike damage scales off the current number of charges in the staff with fixed multipliers of 16 and 4. DiceAmount.resource_spent can express only a 1:1 link to charges spent, not multiplied charge-based damage.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you fail to avoid the effect, you take Force damage equal to 16 times the number of charges in the staff. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to 4 times the number of charges in the staff.

proposed_widenings.name: area_origin.attached_item
proposed_widenings.justification: Retributive Strike's explosion originates from the staff itself. AreaOrigin currently supports point_within_range, on_primary_target, and self, but not an item-originated emanation.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The staff is destroyed and releases its magic in an explosion that fills a 30-foot Emanation originating from itself.

notes: The spell-table, charge pool, and dawn recharge fit existing magic-item activation patterns, but the passive weapon/spell bonuses, nonbinary last-charge rider, and Retributive Strike all require widenings. Because a passive damage-roll bonus is not a v4 atom in the current taxonomy, this is classified as atom_widening rather than surface_widening.
